chunks: Hammad, from Hareyz, from the one who informed him, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) who said:
The menstruating woman prays upon the deceased body because there is no bowing nor prostration in it; and the one with major ritual impurity performs tayammum and prays upon the deceased body.

key_terms.الطَّامِثُ: The menstruating woman (or woman in post-partum bleeding)
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: The one in a state of major ritual impurity (Janabah)
key_terms.تُصَلِّي عَلَى الْجِنَازَةِ: Prays upon the deceased body (Salat al-Janazah)

ai.seo_question: Can a menstruating woman pray upon the deceased in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) derives the permissibility of Salat al-Janazah for women in states of hayd and janabah by focusing on the absence of ruku' and sujud, which are the primary acts requiring purity in standard prayers. This ruling highlights the distinct legal status of the funeral prayer as a non-obligatory (ghayr wajib) act where minor impurity does not invalidate the performance, provided the janib performs tayammum. This perspective is central to Shia fiqh in distinguishing between the conditions of validity for obligatory versus non-obligatory prayers.

en.hubeali:
Hammad, from Hareyz, from the one who informed him, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The menstruating women can pray Salaat upon the deceased because there is neither a bowing in it nor a prostration; and the one with sexual impurity should perform Tayammum and she can pray Salaat upon the deceased’.
en.sarwar: 5. Hammad has narrated from Hariz from those whom he has mentioned who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘

Woman experiencing Hayd (menses) can also perform Salah (prayer) for a deceased; there is no Ruku‘, and Sajdah. One experiencing sexual relation can take Tayammum and performs Salah (prayer) for a deceased.’”
